articles.title: Hudgins, Floyd lead attack strategy as Highland Park beats Frisco Reedy in 5A-I semifinal
articles.summary: Highland Park will attempt to repeat as state champions at the Class 5A Division I state championship match next Saturday.
articles.body:
FRISCO – While studying the tendencies of the Frisco Reedy volleyball team this week, Highland Park outside hitter Allie Hudgins and her teammates came up with a hitting strategy. They figured that placement on kills was more important than velocity. Hudgins and her teammates were sensational in executing their strategy on Saturday.

Hudgins and Sarah Floyd had 14 kills apiece to anchor an attack that frequently found the open spots in the court, especially in the last two sets as Highland Park pulled away for a 27-25, 25-16, 25-15 win over Reedy in a Class 5A Division I state semifinal at the Rock Hill High School Arena. The most pivotal point of the match was the end of set 1 in which Reedy had a 25-24 lead. After a timeout, Highland Park regrouped to score the next three points with Floyd getting two kills in that run.

Hudgins said her team was a little nervous in the first set because of a loud group of Reedy fans behind them in the stands. It was a sentiment echoed by Floyd, a University of Texas pledge who was playing in her fourth playoff match this season after missing most of this season because of an injury suffered in Highland Park's season opener in Aug. 13.

"During the timeout we wanted to make sure we wouldn't get scared or nervous and just go out there and play and see what we can do," Floyd said. "We were looking for tips and off-speed shots."

Highland Park took command of the match in set 2, especially closing it out with an 11-5 run. Leading a team that was taking just a little off on full-swing kills or poking the ball over the Reedy defense at the net, Hudgins had six kills in the second set while Floyd had five kills and two blocks. Highland Park finished with a 52-32 edge in kills for the match.

"We did a really great job in just getting kills. We worked a lot on tipping and getting open spots when we were scouting them," said Hudgins, who signed to play college volleyball at Creighton on Wednesday. "We studied the defense of their setters."

Highland Park (28-12), ranked No. 5 in The Dallas Morning News ' Class 5A-others area poll, will attempt to repeat as state champions at the Class 5A Division I state championship match against Corpus Christi Flour Bluff at 1 p.m. next Saturday at the Curtis Culwell Center in Garland. Highland Park, which regrouped after an 8-11 start this season, improved to 4-0 all-time in state semifinal matches.

No. 4-ranked Reedy (32-7) was denied its second appearance in a state-title match after advancing to the Class 5A final in 2022. Reedy had a 17-match winning streak snapped and has lost its last seven matchups with Highland Park with four as district opponents in 2024 and 2025.

In the third set Floyd had three kills as Highland Park jumped to a 9-3 lead. Taylor Toomay, a Colorado pledge, had five kills in the third set for Highland Park, including the kill to end the match.

Toomay was strong in serving the entire match and finished with four aces, two as part of a 5-0 run in the first set to give Highland Park a 9-8 lead. Highland Park also got a strong setting performance from Anna Lee, who finished with a match-high 41 assists. Highland Park libero Landry Carroll led all players with 14 digs.

"We faced a lot of adversity at the beginning of this season, but I think that prepared us for this," Hudgins said. "You want to be playing your best volleyball at the end of the season, and we are."

Reedy outside hitter and Sam Houston State signee Mariah Akinsola concluded her high school career with 10 kills. Fellow senior and Stonehill signee Bree Benningfield had nine kills, five in the first set.

Reedy setter Karina Crowder had a strong all-around match with 16 assists and 11 digs. Senior libero and Jacksonville University signee Nia LaMons finished with 10 digs.

articles.title: Justin Herbert: Worst Chargers QB fantasy season since Ryan Leaf
articles.summary: In fantasy, Justin Herbert is playing about as well as former Charger Ryan Leaf did 26 years ago. Things have to get better, right?
articles.body:
In fantasy, Justin Herbert is playing about as well as former Chargers quarterback Ryan Leaf did 26 years ago. Things have to get better, right?

Entering this season, the 2000 Chargers were the worst in franchise history. They went 1-15 and then gave up on Leaf, the #2 overall pick in the 1998 draft. In many ways, it's an apples-and-zucchini comparison. Leaf was out of the league within a year. Herbert is in his prime and remains the Chargers' unquestioned starter.

But their numbers are oddly similar, raising the question of whether Herbert and this offense can turn things around. Herbert has averaged 199 passing yards per game while assembling a horrible 0.55 TD-to-interception ratio .38 He's also taken 31 sacks. In his nine starts in 2000, Leaf averaged 192 passing yards while collecting a terrible 0.63 TD-to-interception ratio. He also took 29 sacks.

Herbert is the third Chargers franchise QB to emerge from the ashes of their turn-of-the-century mistake. He, Philip Rivers, and Drew Brees have started all but 12 games in the past 25 seasons. There is no indication that Herbert is post-prime or that this will be a long-term issue.

However, most fantasy managers who drafted Herbert gave up on him a while ago, and for good reasons. So the question remains: will he continue posting Leaf-like numbers the rest of this year? Or will talent eventually rise to the top? Their Monday night matchup in Baltimore will tell us a lot.

articles.title: Celtics Get Timely Paul George Injury Update Ahead of Mavericks Game
articles.summary: The Celtics received a timely Paul George injury update ahead of their Mavericks showdown following his 36-point explosion. The post Celtics Get Timely Paul...
articles.body:
The Boston Celtics are riding a five-game winning streak, and they appear poised to welcome back one of the players who helped build it.

Paul George is no longer listed on Boston's injury report ahead of Sunday's home game against the Dallas Mavericks, putting the veteran forward in position to return after missing Wednesday's victory over the Toronto Raptors because of an illness.

The development comes just four days after George delivered his best performance of the season, scoring 36 points against his former team, the Philadelphia 76ers.

According to the NBA's official injury report, George was not among the Celtics players listed Saturday afternoon.

The Paul George injury update is encouraging for Boston, which enters Sunday's matchup with a 10-2 record.

Although his absence from the report suggests he is available, George's status remains subject to any late changes.

Paul George Injury Update Follows 36-Point Outburst

George missed Wednesday's game in Toronto, one night after putting together a memorable performance in Philadelphia.

The nine-time All-Star scored 36 points on 14-of-22 shooting, including six 3-pointers, as Boston defeated the Sixers, 123-101.

George also grabbed five rebounds in 30 minutes.

His performance proved especially important in the fourth quarter, when Boston turned a competitive game into a rout.

The Celtics opened the period with 14 unanswered points. Payton Pritchard started the run with consecutive 3-pointers before George scored eight straight.

George finished with 14 points in the final quarter, reminding Philadelphia what it lost when the veteran forward departed.

The performance also demonstrated his value alongside Jayson Tatum in Boston's offense.

George provides another experienced scorer who can create his own shot, space the floor and defend multiple positions.

His absence the following night forced Boston to adjust its rotation against Toronto.

Boston Looks to Extend Winning Streak Against Dallas

Boston overcame a 22-point deficit Wednesday to defeat Toronto, 98-93, extending its winning streak to five games.

Tatum led the comeback with 24 points, while Derrick White added 19 and Pritchard contributed 14.

Neemias Queta finished with 11 points and 13 rebounds.

Tatum made the tying and go-ahead free throws with 25.2 seconds remaining, completing Boston's dramatic turnaround.

The Celtics accomplished that without George, but having him back would give coach Joe Mazzulla another offensive option against Dallas.

Boston will host the Mavericks on Sunday at TD Garden, with tipoff scheduled for 6 p.m. ET.

The Celtics' injury report contains no other players sidelined because of injuries or illnesses. Four players are listed as questionable for G League-related reasons.

Dallas, meanwhile, is coming off a difficult start to the season and faces another demanding assignment against one of the Eastern Conference's hottest teams.

For Boston, George's apparent return could strengthen a lineup that has already demonstrated its depth.

And after his 36-point performance in Philadelphia, the Celtics have good reason to want him back on the floor.

articles.title: How Jackson State football can win SWAC East despite Alabama State loss with one game left
articles.summary: Jackson State football lost 20-13 to Alabama State on Nov. 14. The Tigers' path to the SWAC Championship is now harder, but not impossible.
articles.body:
MONTGOMERY, AL – Just a week ago, Jackson State football was riding high.

A win over Mississippi Valley State had put the No. 22 Tigers (7-3, 4-3 SWAC) back in a first-place tie in the SWAC East standings. All they had to do to secure the division title and a spot in the SWAC Championship was win their last two games.

That proved to be too tall a task for JSU, as it lost 20-13 to Alabama State (6-4, 4-3) at ASU Stadium on Nov. 14.

The Tigers and Hornets are now tied for second place behind Alabama A&M (8-2, 5-2), meaning JSU will have to rely on AAMU to lose another game.

"Finish strong," JSU coach T.C. Taylor said. "That's what I just told the team. Get your head up. Wipe your blood off your mouth, and let's just go finish strong, and we'll see how it falls when that's done."

Can Jackson State still win the SWAC East?

JSU no longer has a chance to win the division outright. If JSU wins its final game against Alcorn State (6-5, 4-3) on Nov. 21 and Alabama A&M loses its finale to MVSU (3-8, 2-5), the Tigers will still be eligible to make the conference championship game. They'd be reliant on tiebreakers to get them there.

If they end the season in a two-way tie with the Bulldogs, JSU has the head-to-head win over AAMU and would win the division.

However, there could be a three-way tie for first place if Alabama State wins its final SWAC game against Prairie View A&M (6-5, 5-2).

The first multi-team tiebreaker, head-to-head results, would not provide an answer since JSU beat AAMU, AAMU beat Alabama State and Alabama State beat JSU.

The next tiebreaker is record against division opponents. JSU is 3-2 against SWAC East teams, AAMU is 3-1, and Alabama State is 2-3.

In this scenario that has AAMU losing to MVSU, the Bulldogs would finish 3-2 against the SWAC East.

With Alabama State eliminated from the tie, the fist tiebreaker used to decide a division winner between AAMU and JSU would be head-to-head competition, which would give JSU the win.

What went wrong for Jackson State vs Alabama State

JSU's final game is a road contest vs. Alcorn State, the conference's best offense.

"Their offense is explosive," Taylor said. "They're playing at a high level right now. … All we can do is get back in here tomorrow and just finish this thing strong, trying to finish 8-3."

With their season on the line against the Braves, JSU cannot afford to make the same mistakes it did against Alabama State.

The Tigers were their own worst enemy, turning the ball over three times, including an interception in the end zone thrown by quarterback Jared Lockhart with six seconds left in the game that solidified the loss.

Lockhart also lost a fumble in the third quarter that cut a JSU drive short just past midfield. The Tigers went scoreless in that period.

"Just him trying to make plays," Taylor said of the fumble. "You tell him and talk to him about it because at the quarterback position, he's going to touch the ball every play and can't fault him for that. It just happened. He did a good job of shaking it off and trying to get us in a position towards the end to win the game."

The other turnover, a fumble by tight end Jency Riley Jr., happened in the first quarter and was returned by Alabama State for a touchdown. That ultimately proved to be the difference, considering both offenses scored 13 points.

JSU also turned the ball over twice on downs, one of which led to a Hornets' field goal in the fourth quarter.

"Anytime Alabama State and Jackson State link up, that's what you're going to get, a good battle right there," Taylor said. "But, just thinking back on it, turned the ball over too many times offensively. … Defense played, they gave us a chance to win the game, but you've got to find ways to generate points, and we didn't do that."

JSU did not make any players available to speak to media.

Tia Reid covers Jackson State sports for the Clarion Ledger . Email her at treid@usatodayco.com and follow her on X @tiareid65 .

articles.title: Suns’ Jordan Goodwin Isn’t Backing Down From Luka Doncic in Lakers Showdown
articles.summary: The Phoenix Suns have found their footing after a rough start, and Sunday brings one of their toughest tests yet. The red-hot Los Angeles Lakers are coming t...
articles.body:
The Phoenix Suns have found their footing after a rough start, and Sunday brings one of their toughest tests yet. The red-hot Los Angeles Lakers are coming to town, and one Suns guard already knows how he wants that night to go.

He isn't the biggest name on the roster. But he knows the Lakers' star better than most, having shared a locker room with him not long ago.

Jordan Goodwin, who played alongside Luka Doncic in Los Angeles, was asked how he plans to guard his former teammate. The Arizona Republic's Duane Rankin shared his answer on X.

"Just got to go out there and compete. Luka's a great player, can put the ball in the hole. Can manipulate the game with fouls and his savvy play, but I'm just going to be myself. Attack him how I attack everybody else. Watch my film. I'm just going to check the ball up," Goodwin said.

Goodwin was also asked about the trash talk. Doncic loves to chirp at defenders, and Goodwin expects plenty of it. But he made it clear there is no bad blood.

"Luka and I, we're real cool. We're real close. We were close out in L.A. We always talk. It's going to be talking crazy, but it's going to be respectful basketball. It's going to be good bump. We'll see. If he starts talking, he starts talking, but we'll see how the game goes," Goodwin said.

From Waived by the Lakers to a Key Piece in Phoenix

There's a reason this one means a little more to Goodwin. The Lakers waived him in the summer of 2025, and the Suns claimed him off waivers. It turned out to be a steal for Phoenix.

Last season, he brought defense and timely shooting off the bench. He averaged 8.7 points and 4.9 rebounds in 70 games while hitting 37.1 percent from three.

His best night came in the Play-In Tournament, when he put up 19 points, nine rebounds, and six steals against the Golden State Warriors while hounding Stephen Curry. This summer, Phoenix gave him a three-year, $19 million deal.

Goodwin will need all of that defense on Sunday. The good news for Phoenix is that he's back. He missed four games with a calf injury before returning Tuesday, when he hit six of seven threes in a win over the Clippers .

Doncic leads the NBA in scoring at 38.6 points per game, along with 7.5 rebounds and 7.6 assists. The Lakers are 11-2 and riding a seven-game win streak.

Doncic turned his ankle late in Wednesday's win over the Bucks, but coach JJ Redick said Friday the star is fine and expected to play.

The Suns, meanwhile, sit at 5-6 and have won four of their last five after a 1-5 start.

Tip-off is set for 4 p.m. ET at Mortgage Matchup Center.

Goodwin says he will check the ball up and play his game. On Sunday, Phoenix finds out who gets the last word.

articles.title: Kyle Whittingham heckled by Michigan football fans after Oregon loss
articles.summary: Michigan coach Kyle Whittingham faces fan backlash after a tough loss and a struggling season for the Wolverines.
articles.body:
If Kyle Whittingham thought he was going to have some quiet contemplation as he worked to figure out how to fix Michigan football, he would be wrong.

The former Utah coach took over a 9-3 Michigan football team that currently sits at 5-5 and looks to be in real danger of missing a bowl game, unless it can win against undefeated UCLA and then on the road at Ohio State . The dust hadn't even begun to settle from his worst drubbing as the Wolverines head coach yet, a 31-7 loss at Oregon , before he started hearing it from fans of the program he coaches -- 2,000 miles away from his current home.

According to The Athletic's Austin Meek, Whittingham was heckled after leaving his postgame press conference by Michigan fans who were in attendance at the game. They had apparently waited around to get the opportunity to voice their displeasure with the direction of the program personally.

Whittingham did eventually change the program's direction this past Sunday when he fired offensive coordinator Jason Beck, and while the offense used scheme and formation more suitable for the players on the roster, they were able to muster just seven points against the Ducks.

articles.title: Today in White Sox History: November 14
articles.summary: Chris Sale begins a seven-season streak of Cy Young support
articles.body:
1900 The aggressively-improving American League was rejected as an equal major league by the established National League. Although there were multiple major leagues more often than not in the course of organized baseball over the latter half of the 19th Century, at this juncture the NL felt it was the sole top circuit in the game, and it was especially irked that the AL was ignoring the National Agreement to compete head-to-head in NL cities like Baltimore, Philadelphia and Washington, D.C.

How did this affect the White Sox , a newly-formed AL team relocating from St. Paul? The 1900 pennant, the first awarded by the new league, was won by the White Sox, whose 82-53 record was 4 1 ⁄ 2 games better than the Milwaukee Brewers . But it, along with the records of the 1900 players, are not consider "major league"; Baseball-Reference, for example, begins its White Sox franchise history at 1901, the first year the AL was regarded as "major."

However, the White Sox had just four of 28 players without prior major league experience, and half of the players cut from the National League (the circuit had shrunk from 12 to eight teams for 1900) ended up in the AL, legitimizing its major status. And before the season had even begun, the Chicago Tribune observed that "the American League is not, after all, much behind the old, cumbersome National League."

The 1900 triumph was the first pennant won by a Chicago team in 14 years.

The White Sox, mostly intact and even bolstered from 1900, went back-to-back in winning the AL pennant in 1901, the first season the AL was considered a major league. In fact, Frank Isbell , Roy Patterson , Ed McFarland played on the 1900 and 1901 pennant winners and 1906 World Series winners.

1977 The move was overshadowed by the failure of Ron Blomberg (signed three days later) falling flat as heir apparent slugger after the South Side Hit Men season, but in some sense, signing pitcher Jim Hughes hit harder. Injuries limited Hughes to just two games out of the pen in 1977, making him a perfect candidate for Bill Veeck 's shoestring Rent-a-Player scheme; plus, perhaps Hughes would fare as well as Twins third baseman Eric Soderholm did for the White Sox under similar circumstances a year earlier. However, Hughes was cut at the end of Spring Training and never pitched a single game for the White Sox, or any other MLB team, after that.

1995 On the strength of a career-best 2.2 WAR season while working off of a prove-it, one-year deal, Dave Martinez re-signed with the White Sox for two years and what turned out to be just shy of $2 million.

Martinez did not sit back after getting paid, putting up a stellar 4.4 WAR season in 1996 and getting on base nearly 40% of the time. While that year would stand as the very best of Martinez's 16 years in the majors, he followed it with his second-best season, 3.1 WAR in 1997. All told, the outfielder's three best career years came in his three years with the White Sox.

And somehow, the club didn't interview him for its manager role after Ozzie Guillén bolted Chicago in 2011.

2012 Chris Sale finished sixth in AL Cy Young voting, the first of seven straight years he would finish in the Top 6. Sale, on the strength of 5.7 WAR, a 17-8 record, 3.05 ERA/3.27 FIP, 1.135 WHIP and 192 strikeouts, earned 17 votes, an 11% share. The battle for the award itself was very tight, with David Price edging out Justin Verlander, 153-149.

In all five of Sale's starting seasons on the South Side, he earned Cy Young votes.

2024 White Sox All-Star lefthander Garrett Crochet was named the American League Comeback Player of the Year.

Crochet, 25, was 6-12 with a 3.58 ERA and 209 strikeouts in 32 starts and 146 innings in 2024, his first season as a starter after missing most of 2023 while recovering from Tommy John surgery. In fact, he joined a short list of players in baseball history when he made his first career start on Opening Day.

Among pitchers with at least 140 innings, Crochet led the A.L. in strikeouts with 12.88 per nine innings and was second in strikeout-to-walk ratio (6.33).

Crochet became the third Sox player to win the Comeback award, joining righthander Liam Hendriks in 2023 and designated hitter Jim Thome in 2006.

Alas, less than a month after receiving the honor, Crochet was dealt to Boston as the headliner in a five-player swap.

articles.title: Ethically Questionable Journalist ‘Bets’ Big On Super Bowl Return
articles.summary: Dianna Russini seeks a high-profile Radio Row spot at the Super Bowl despite her recent scandal and ties to an unregulated book.
articles.body:
Dianna Russini is making a bold push to return to the center of the NFL media world this February. During Super Bowl week in Los Angeles, she seeks a prime location on Radio Row. Front Office Sports reported on Friday that she is actively seeking this high-profile role. The move to seek the high-profile role comes just months after she stepped down from The Athletic following a very public scandal. Russini is hosting a new show with BetUS, an offshore book that lacks U.S. regulation . The league often does not recognize such outlets as sources of official media credentials. To get around this hurdle, she plans to apply using her connection to iHeartMedia instead. She is set to host a podcast on that platform with Jon Weiner soon.

Russini resigned in April after Page Six released intimate photos of her and Patriots coach Mike Vrabel. The pictures showed them holding hands at a resort in Arizona back in March. Both Russini and Vrabel are married to other people. The Athletic launched an investigation, and Vrabel took a leave to get counseling. Russini, 43, has stayed quiet until her return to the media last week. She debuted "The Russini Report" and even joked about the memes the scandal created. She did not spend much time talking about her relationship with Vrabel during the launch. Her path back is complicated by the nature of her new employer and the league's strict rules.

She finally opened up about the pain of the last few months in a story with People magazine. "The best way to describe what the last six months were like for me is heartbreaking," Russini said. She described the lies as getting out of control and called the situation a runaway train. She explained that reading the news became unhealthy and only added to the pain they were already dealing with. Russini never explained exactly what she claims were the lies, but the impact was clear. The scandal forced her out of a top job and into a period of silence.

The NFL controls who gets on Radio Row, and they are known for being very picky. They prefer major networks and established outlets over new or offshore ventures. Russini's ties to BetUS could be why she gets shut out despite her experience. If the league denies her request, it would be a major blow to her new venture. The Super Bowl in Los Angeles is set for February, and the media schedule is already taking shape.

According to reports, Russini intends to secure a credential via her iHeartMedia affiliation.

articles.title: Could an actor have subconsciously predicted the 2027 MLB season?
articles.summary: A stage play offers an unexpected glimpse into baseball’s uncertain future
articles.body:
Richard Greenberg's play "Take Me Out" was such a superb and intense work that it not only won the 2003 Best Play Tony Award and many others when it first ran on Broadway, but also the Tony Award for Best Revival of a Play 19 years later. Greenberg, who died last year, was a terrific writer, even if he did have the major failing of being a Yankees fan. But we should probably forgive him for that now, what with him being deceased and all.

"Take Me Out" is a baseball play, centering on the New York Empires (get it?) and their star center fielder, Darren Lemming, who decides to announce in the middle of a season that he's gay.

That sets off a lot of drama as some teammates support him, some excoriate him — one with tragic consequences — and others just try to steer clear. The team falters as it splits on the matter, but recovers in time to — this is the pseudo-Yankees of a few decades ago, remember — win the World Series.

"How does that predict 2027?" you may ask. Which is a fair question. For that, we need to get to a specific production and even a specific performance of that production. And consider what is about to happen at the end of this month.

In the course of the season, Lemming acquires a nebbish accountant and later friend named Mason Marzac, who at the start has no interest in baseball wins or losses, just spreadsheet assets and liabilities. Naturally, Marzac, in a role that won a Tony Award for best featured actor in a play for Northwestern grad Denis O'Hare (now probably best known as Stanley in "American Horror Story"), becomes a huge fan. So much of one that, as he and Lemming are the last ones to leave the locker room after the final World Series win, he turns back to the room (and the audience, of course) and wistfully wonders, "What will we do until spring?"

But how does this get us to 2027, for crying out loud?

I was working for the Human Race Theatre in Dayton when it produced "Take Me Out" in Spring 2007. Come opening night, all went well except for the fact that in the game scenes, the actor playing the Japanese pitcher couldn't for the life of him be cajoled, ordered or otherwise convinced to throw with his foot on the rubber — he pitched from behind the rubber the entire run of the play, clearly seen by the audience seated around the stage. Chances are nobody but a few of us who had tried to get him to start out correctly even noticed, so it was a minor matter, but a flaw nonetheless.

Not yet. We have to come to the end of the play.

Picture Lemming and Marzac, season over, World Series won, hate and discontent behind them. Brian McKnight, a Human Race resident artist with strong Chicago ties (including an MFA from DePaul), played Marzac. He's a fine, solid actor.

As they exit the locker room, he turns back and with proper wistfulness says, "What will we do until (pause) (pause) summer?"

Now, probably only those of us who knew the script noticed the change of seasons, so it was no biggie. I kidded Brian about it later, and he said he had a brain freeze and was lucky to get any word out. He was mortified — it happens to most actors on occasion.

Notice that was precisely 20 years before the upcoming season, a season that may well not begin in the spring (or even summer?) thanks to the greed of a nonagenarian control freak who despises players for taking too much of his money and fans for not giving him enough of theirs (see, there is a White Sox connection here, after all) and his five co-conspirators on the owners' negotiating team.

So did Brian just suffer a momentary mental lapse? Or did he somehow foresee what is soon to come, to the dismay of all of us fans?

articles.title: How Missouri State football won its first home OT game in history
articles.summary: Joel Boamah and Dylan Brooks score defensive touchdowns in Missouri State's OT win versus New Mexico State. Why the Bears are so great at defensive scores.
articles.body:
SPRINGFIELD — Missouri State (4-6, 3-3 in CUSA) relied on defensive prowess and a bit of luck in a homecoming thriller on Saturday, Nov. 14.

The Bears defeated New Mexico State 27-21 in overtime. This was Missouri State's first home overtime win in history. The Bears were previously 0-4 in such games.

In a play that will be seen by many across social media, Joel Boamah came away with the game-winning pick-six in overtime. Boamah jumped the pass and took it to the house for an 88-yard touchdown, winning the game without Missouri State's offense touching the field in overtime.

"It felt good making plays for the team to win. It was a great way to cap a good win for homecoming," Boamah said. "I played my technique and trusted my coaches and made a play on the ball."

Missouri State football hosts New Mexico State in annual homecoming game

Scoring on defense has been a staple for Missouri State this season. Along with Boamah's game-winner, defensive lineman Dylan Brooks dropped back into coverage and snagged a running back screen. Brooks took the pick to the end zone from 15 yards away for the first score of the game.

"Those momentum plays are what we fight for, what we play for, it's what we coach," Missouri State coach Casey Woods said.

Missouri State has now scored five defensive touchdowns this season. The defense scored against FIU, Delaware and SMU. It's not just happenstance, defesive touchdowns are a major skillset for the team.

Entering this week, Alabama and Texas Tech were tied for the most defensive touchdowns with five. Missouri State will enter next week tied with the nation leaders or close to it.

"We have a good camaraderie within the defense. We are always together and we are always talking about how we can do better within the play," Boamah said. "We play together as a tight-knit unit."

Why was Missouri State lucky in the win?

New Mexico State missed a 22-yard chip shot field goal with 2:51 left in the game. The Aggies would have gone ahead by 10 points, instead Missouri State marched down the field for the game-tying touchdown.

Woods didn't necessarily call the play lucky. He chalked it up to a missed opportunity, which can occur on any given play. The missed field goal certainly gave the Bears life.

Missouri State's final drive featured some big throws from quarterback Henry Belin to star wide receiver Isaiah Myers. It was all capped off with a short rushing touchdown by Connor Lair.

"The energy on the sideline, knowing we had to make a play," Lair said. "The defense has our back all game, we owed it to them."

Missouri State's offense only accumulated 292 yards. It was a clunky game with Lair's touchdown and a passing score from Belin to Jmariyae Robins as the offense's only points.

Lair said the team needs to play more complementary football and help the defense at all costs. The Aggies went just 5-for-15 on third down. They also had a fumble, missed field goal and Boamah's game-winning touchdown in the red zone.

"It sucks not playing complementary football and help out the defense," Lair said. "They held on long enough and we showed up when it mattered."

Missouri State's destiny is still in its own hands. But it won't be easy.

The Bears face the conference's top two teams to close out the regular season. They will go on the road to Jacksonville State (7-3, 5-1) next week. Missouri State has failed to win a road game this year and will need to play its best ball against the Gamecocks.

Missouri State closes its regular season at home against league-leader Liberty (9-1, 6-0) on Saturday, Nov. 28.

"We are playing meaningful games in November. We are in bowl contention," Woods said. "This is something Missouri State's dreamed about for a lot of years is being a consistent FBS team."

Liam Keating covers high school sports and Missouri State athletics for The Springfield News-Leader. Send stats or information to him at Lkeating@usatodayco.com

articles.title: Kickoff time, TV designation revealed for Michigan Football vs UCLA
articles.summary: Here is the kickoff time and TV designation for Michigan Football’s Senior Day matchup vs UCLA:
articles.body:
The Michigan Wolverines return from Oregon next week to host UCLA on Senior Day. The Big Ten released the kickoff times and TV designations for just a few of the Week 12 games earlier this week, but Michigan-UCLA was not one of them.

Well, now we have the answers that we were looking for. As (finally) announced by the Big Ten, Michigan vs UCLA will start at 3:30 p.m. and be aired on CBS.

The Game between Michigan and Ohio State was already scheduled to kickoff at noon and be aired on FOX, so we now know the kickoff times and TV designations for the final two games for the Wolverines this season.

Led by first-year head coach Bob Chesney, UCLA is playing its best season of college football since the 2010s when it had back-to-back 10-win seasons in 2013 and 2014. In fact, the Bruins have never won more than 10 games in a single season, so this might be the year they pull that off. They are coming off a 22-14 win over Illinois on Friday night that advanced their record to 10-0 on the season.

Michigan is 8-3 in the all-time series against UCLA. The last time Michigan played UCLA was in 2000, a 23-20 loss in Pasadena. Michigan last hosted the Bruins in 1996, which was a 38-9 blowout win for the Wolverines.

articles.title: Lakers’ Austin Reaves ruled out for upcoming clash vs. Suns
articles.summary: Coach JJ Redick’s Los Angeles Lakers are 11-2 on the season and preparing to face Jordan Ott’s 11th place Phoenix team, shortly after comments made by Ziaire...
articles.body:
Coach JJ Redick 's Los Angeles Lakers are 11-2 on the season and preparing to face Jordan Ott's 11th place Phoenix team, shortly after comments made by Ziaire Williams about a former Suns teammate . Redick made a surprising comment about a Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves off-court obsession that gave fans pause.

Prior to Sunday's game, Dave McMenamin of ESPN gave a Lakers injury update . Reaves has a left heel bruise and is expected to miss Sunday, November 15's game while Cameron Carr has an illness and is also listed as 'out.'

Bronny James Jr. is questionable with an illness, as is Collin Sexton with a right orbital laceration. Adou Thiero is questionable with a left ankle sprain.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The game is schedule for 4 p.m. ET and will put the Lakers' 6-1 road record to the test. The Suns are 5-3 at home, and the two teams have won their last nine games combined, including seven in a row from Redick's Lakers.

Doncic's performance could determine whether LA sinks or swims with Reaves out for the game. The Suns are led by Devin Booker, who has scored 20 or more points in seven of his last games, including four 30-point games.

Reaves has also been on a tear, with 25.5 points per game on average in the month of November.

Doncic and the Lakers have the firepower to beat the Suns on the road, but it's going to take a team effort. Doncic can supply enough extra points to shoot down Ott's team, but his teammates must play smart basketball, and do the dirty work, if LA is to escape the Valley of the Sun with another victory. Quetin Grimes has stepped up lately , giving Redick and his team hope for a big W against Phoenix, even without Reaves.

articles.title: Five finals, one first: Luvanga and ‘Rowdy Audi’ lift Spirit to home NWSL Championship berth
articles.summary: WASHINGTON — Clara Luvanga has been here before. Six days ago, to be exact. The 21-year-old Tanzanian striker saw her opening, as a clumsy pass back to Utah...
articles.body:
WASHINGTON — Clara Luvanga has been here before. Six days ago, to be exact.

The 21-year-old Tanzanian striker saw her opening, as a clumsy pass back to Utah Royals goalkeeper Mandy McGlynn sputtered into open space. Luvanga spent the match pressing high for precisely these moments. She had put similar pressure on the Portland Thorns defense in the Washington Spirit's 4-1 quarterfinal win a week earlier.

Against seventh-seeded Utah, all she needed was a quick touch to score her second playoff goal since signing with the Spirit in September, sending Audi Field, aka "Rowdy Audi," into chaos.

Luvanga's 56th-minute winner secured a 2-1 victory for the Spirit, helping Washington secure its third consecutive trip to the NWSL Championship. It also marks the first time the Spirit will be playing in a championship at home and a record-tying fifth appearance in the league final.

"The impact that she's made has been unbelievable," Spirit goalkeeper Sandy MacIver said. "Pretty much every game she's been a part of, she's made something happen. A one-goal game, and she gets it just from a work ethic — to track down that ball, and then the technical ability and execution to put in that goal was world-class."

The former Al-Nassr FC forward has been the spark the Spirit needed in the postseason, bringing out the best in some of the team's biggest stars.

She was a key contributor in their quarterfinal blowout over Portland, scoring a goal and recording two assists. On Saturday, Luvanga's transitional play in the midfield helped the build-up play that led to Sofia Cantore's back-heel equalizer in the eighth minute, muting an impressive Olimpico scored by Utah's Cloé Lacasse directly from a corner kick just five minutes earlier.

"We haven't been together that long, so we're still learning from each other and figuring out, like, where we want to receive the ball, and our distances apart from each other," said Spirit forward Trinity Rodman. "It's been really good. Obviously, me and (Cantore) already have a really good connection, so we're just building out with (players like) Mélissa (Bethi) and Clara."

The Spirit roster includes a mix of longtime players and new faces such as Luvanga, Bethi and Monique Ngock, who all joined the club this year on multi-year contracts. They mix in with more established players such as Rodman and captain Andi Sullivan, who are entering the final week of the postseason in phenomenal form after coming back from injuries in recent years. Sullivan's absence was extended when she took maternity leave in 2025.

Rodman described Sullivan as the "glue" that keeps their team together.

"She brings something on the field that not a lot of players bring," Rodman said. "Her intensity, the way that she can attack, the way that she defends in every area of the field — like, she's everywhere. And I think for her, it's just — she's just so happy."

Sullivan, who missed the last two finals, will get to appear in her first for the team since 2021, when the Spirit lifted their first trophy.

"I think it hit her today," Rodman said. "Just knowing we're going to the final, that she's played a really big part in us getting there, and a bigger role than she had previously played in years past. I'm really proud of her, really happy, and having her on the field is really good for our team, too."

The Spirit win brought an end to Utah's historic season, which included their first postseason run since joining the NWSL in 2018.

The Royals adopted a "why not us?" mentality in their playoff run, after shocking the league by upsetting No. 2 San Diego Wave FC in their postseason debut. The result reshuffled the postseason standings, allowing the Spirit to host every round of playoffs at home this year.

"This is a good group of soccer players who have grinded and have experience in this league and deserve all the success they're getting this year," Utah defender Kate Del Fava said. "Together, we have accomplished something that no one thought we could except us, and that's fine for us, but we want the league to know that we deserve to be here."

The Spirit are now the first team in NWSL history to reach five championship games without relocating. The Western New York Flash/North Carolina Courage franchise has pulled off the same feat, accumulating trophies in New York before relocating and winning more in North Carolina.

"First day of preseason, you talked about wanting to be in the final and wanting to win the championship, and then you have to let go of it and break it down day by day and week by week," Sullivan said. "To see that reward payoff is really satisfying, and speaks to how important it is to stick to the process."

That reward means the Spirit will return to Audi Field next week, where they face the winner of the semifinal match between Kansas City Current and Gotham FC.

The Spirit will be looking to become only the second team in league history to lift a championship trophy at home (after the Courage did it in 2019). Against Utah, the Spirit played before a sellout crowd of 19,365 people — their sixth consecutive postseason sellout. Next weekend's final will likely extend that streak to a seventh straight sellout.

That "Rowdy Audi" energy makes Washington a hard place to play for any visiting team. That was evident when the Spirit were down so early in the game, and the crowd roared with every counterattack from the home team as they rallied for an equalizer.

"It's not just about the goals," Sullivan said. "It's about the heart, and that's what you want. These fans understand us, and they respect big plays, and plays where small little details make a huge difference, they're roaring, and that gives you a boost.

"It helps us give more, and then they love it more, and then we give more," Sullivan added. "So, I think it's just this cyclical thing that builds and builds and builds, and (I'm) extremely grateful."
